items.meaning: the core action meaning before affixes
items.example: kaon → mokaon, nikaon, nagkaon
items.natural: eat → will eat, ate, is eating
items.hint: Start by finding the root. Cebuano affixes add aspect, focus, mood, and other meanings around it.

items.meaning: actor-focused action that is not yet begun, intended, or habitual in context
items.example: Mokaon ko ugma.
items.natural: I will eat tomorrow.
items.hint: Time words and context complete the meaning. Mo- is not a simple one-to-one English future tense.

items.meaning: actor-focused completed action
items.example: Nikaon ko kagahapon.
items.natural: I ate yesterday.
items.hint: Ni- and mi- vary by verb, speaker, and region. A time expression such as kagahapon makes the completed reading clear.

items.meaning: actor-focused action viewed as ongoing, progressive, or extended
items.example: Nagkaon ko karon.
items.natural: I am eating now.
items.hint: Nag- can have broader uses, but pairing it with karon gives a clear beginner progressive pattern.

items.meaning: deliberate, planned, habitual, progressive, or command-like actor form depending on context
items.example: Magtuon ko karong gabii.
items.natural: I will study tonight.
items.hint: Mag- belongs to a different verb class from simple mo- forms. Learn common verbs in complete sentences rather than attaching it mechanically to every root.

items.meaning: can, is able to, or gets the opportunity to do an action
items.example: Makasulti ko og gamayng Binisaya.
items.natural: I can speak a little Bisaya.
items.hint: Maka- often expresses ability or successful opportunity, not merely future time.

items.meaning: was able to, managed to, or reached a resulting state
items.example: Nakat-on ko og Binisaya.
items.natural: I learned / have learned Bisaya.
items.hint: Naka- frequently presents an achieved result or completed ability. The exact English translation depends on the root and context.

items.meaning: completed action with the affected item or goal in focus
items.example: Gipalit nako ang tubig.
items.natural: I bought the water. / The water was bought by me.
items.hint: With gi-, the ang phrase is the affected item in focus. The actor commonly appears as nako, nimo, niya, or a name marked by ni.

items.meaning: not-yet, intended, or contemplated action with the goal in focus
items.example: Paliton nako ang tubig.
items.natural: I will buy the water.
items.hint: The suffix may change shape with some roots. Learn each common form with its full sentence pattern.

items.meaning: puts a transferred, used, or conveyed item in focus in many common verbs
items.example: Ihatag nako kini nimo.
items.natural: I will give this to you.
items.hint: I- has several focus functions. Begin with high-frequency transfer expressions such as ihatag rather than treating it as one English preposition.

items.meaning: will eat / ate / is eating
items.example: Mokaon ko ugma. Nikaon ko kagahapon. Nagkaon ko karon.
items.natural: I will eat tomorrow. I ate yesterday. I am eating now.
items.hint: The time words make the beginner contrast clear. In natural discourse, context can carry much of the timing.

items.meaning: will drink / drank / is drinking
items.example: Moinom ko og tubig. Niinom ko ganina. Nag-inom siya karon.
items.natural: I will drink water. I drank earlier. He or she is drinking now.
items.hint: Vowel-initial roots can create adjacent vowels in writing, as in moinom and niinom.

items.meaning: will go / went
items.example: Moadto ko sa merkado. Niadto ko kagahapon.
items.natural: I will go to the market. I went yesterday.
items.hint: Adto refers to going away or over there. Directional vocabulary varies with the speaker’s and listener’s location.

items.meaning: will buy / bought / is buying
items.example: Mopalit ko og tubig. Nipalit ko kagahapon.
items.natural: I will buy water. I bought some yesterday.
items.hint: These are actor-focused forms. Compare them with gipalit and paliton when the bought item is in focus.

items.meaning: will study / is studying / learned
items.example: Magtuon ko. Nagtuon ko karon. Nakat-on ko og Binisaya.
items.natural: I will study. I am studying now. I learned Bisaya.
items.hint: Not every English-related meaning uses the same affix family. Study and learn are best memorised through these common forms.

items.meaning: will speak or say / spoke or said / is speaking
items.example: Mosulti ko og Binisaya. Misulti siya kagahapon.
items.natural: I will speak Bisaya. He or she spoke yesterday.
items.hint: Sulti covers speak, say, or tell depending on its complements and context.

items.meaning: will watch or look / is watching / will watch or examine it
items.example: Magtan-aw ko og sine. Gitan-aw nako ang sine.
items.natural: I will watch a movie. I watched the movie.
items.hint: Tan-aw combines with different affixes and sometimes mag- or mo- patterns depending on the intended construction and variety.

items.meaning: will give as actor / was given / will give this item
items.example: Mohatag ko og tubig. Gihatag nako ang tubig. Ihatag nako kini nimo.
items.natural: I will give water. I gave the water. I will give this to you.
items.hint: The different forms change which participant is highlighted. Learn the marker pattern together with the verb.

items.meaning: will not or does not / did not or was not doing / do not!
items.example: Dili ko mokaon ugma. Wala ko mokaon kagahapon. Ayaw kaon ana.
items.natural: I will not eat tomorrow. I did not eat yesterday. Don’t eat that.
items.hint: Dili commonly negates non-factual or habitual actions, wala negates completed or progressive actions, and ayaw negates commands.

items.meaning: now / yesterday / tomorrow
items.example: Nagkaon karon. Nikaon kagahapon. Mokaon ugma.
items.natural: Eating now. Ate yesterday. Will eat tomorrow.
items.hint: Cebuano aspect forms work with time words and discourse context. The time word often removes ambiguity for a beginner.

dialogue.title: At Verb Volcano
dialogue.note: The dialogue contrasts completed, ongoing, and not-yet actor forms, then introduces a goal-focused -on form. The time words make the aspect contrast visible.

lines.speaker: B
lines.natural: Not yet. I’m going to eat now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Paliton nako ang pancit. Moinom pud ko og tubig.
lines.literal: Buy-ON by-me [FOCUS] pancit. MO-drink also I [OBJ] water.
lines.natural: I’ll buy the pancit. I’ll also drink water.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sige. Human mokaon, magtuon ta og Binisaya.
lines.literal: Okay. After MO-eat, MAG-study we-inclusive [OBJ] Bisaya.
lines.natural: Okay. After eating, let’s study Bisaya.
